professionalSummary.text: Over two years, led daily break‑handling for Visa and Mastercard settlements, maintained runbooks, onboarded analysts, and coordinated escalations with treasury and merchant services.
professionalSummary.witness: Ran the daily break-handling procedure for Visa and Mastercard settlement files at a regional acquirer, working through the break queue in the reconciliation tool and ticking off the control checklist before the 11:00 treasury cut-off.

experienceHighlights.text: Rewrote the reconciliation runbook post‑tool migration, adding screenshots and training two new analysts within their first fortnight.
experienceHighlights.witness: Rewrote the reconciliation runbook after the tool migration, adding screenshots for the new break-classification screen, and walked two newly hired analysts through it during their first fortnight.

experienceHighlights.text: Documented month‑end close notes, listing carried‑over breaks, reasons, and analyst ownership.
experienceHighlights.witness: Wrote the month-end close notes for the reconciliation queue, listing carried-over breaks, the reason each was open and the analyst taking it over.

projectsAndWorkSamples.text: Revised runbook section on break classification and month‑end close note with ticket identifiers as verification trail.
projectsAndWorkSamples.witness: Work sample: the revised runbook section on break classification and one month-end close note with carried-over breaks, with the reconciliation tool's ticket identifiers as a verification trail.

skills.text: Process ownership, runbook maintenance, analyst training, escalation coordination, documentation of limitations and hand‑over conditions.
skills.witness: Responsibilities included break handling, runbook maintenance, analyst onboarding and escalation for the settlement reconciliation queue over about two years.

optimizedCv.evidenceBoundary: The provided resume and work samples establish the candidate’s experience with daily break handling, runbook maintenance, analyst onboarding, escalation coordination, and month‑end documentation. They do not provide quantitative evidence of reducing average time to clear a settlement break or a documented improvement against a published baseline.

decisionBoundary.statement: Candidate has demonstrated relevant process ownership and documentation skills but lacks evidence of measurable time‑to‑clear improvement.

evidence.text: Ran the daily break-handling procedure for Visa and Mastercard settlement files at a regional acquirer, working through the break queue in the reconciliation tool and ticking off the control checklist before the 11:00 treasury cut-off.
evidence.notes: Direct statement of daily procedure and checklist usage.

evidence.text: Rewrote the reconciliation runbook after the tool migration, adding screenshots for the new break-classification screen, and walked two newly hired analysts through it during their first fortnight.

Candidate said that after the runbook rewrite breaks were 'cleared roughly 40 percent faster'; he thought the figure came from a team meeting slide but did not know the baseline or the period it covered.
evidence.notes: Unverified claim, no baseline or period.

missingEvidence: Quantitative data on average time to clear a settlement break, baseline comparison, period of measurement

evidence.text: Raised unresolved breaks above the agreed threshold to treasury and merchant services through the escalation form; the decision to hold or release a merchant payout stayed with the treasury manager.
Wrote the month-end close notes for the reconciliation queue, listing carried-over breaks, the reason each was open and the analyst taking it over.

supportedClaims.claim: Over two years, the candidate has owned daily break handling, runbook maintenance, analyst onboarding, escalation coordination, and month‑end documentation for Visa and Mastercard settlements.
supportedClaims.witness: Ran the daily break-handling procedure for Visa and Mastercard settlement files at a regional acquirer, working through the break queue in the reconciliation tool and ticking off the control checklist before the 11:00 treasury cut-off.

unsupportedClaims.claim: The candidate has demonstrably reduced the average time to clear settlement breaks by 40% compared to the published baseline.
unsupportedClaims.reason: The claim is based on an unverified recollection of a slide; no baseline, period, or measurement is provided.
unsupportedClaims.requiredFollowUp: Provide documented metrics showing average time to clear before and after the runbook rewrite, including the baseline period and the method of calculation.

missingEvidenceGaps.gap: Quantitative evidence of time‑to‑clear improvement, including baseline, period, and calculation method.

interviewSignalRisks.text: Candidate claimed a 40% faster clearance but lacked knowledge of baseline or period.
interviewSignalRisks.recommendedHandling: Verify with data from the reconciliation tool and confirm the baseline period.

followUpQuestions.question: Can you provide the specific metrics that show the average time to clear settlement breaks before and after the runbook rewrite, including the baseline period and how the calculation was performed?
followUpQuestions.evidenceTarget: Quantitative time‑to‑clear data and baseline documentation.

humanReviewChecklist: Confirm that the candidate’s daily break handling aligns with the 11:00 treasury cut‑off requirement.
Verify the runbook rewrite and training evidence against internal documentation standards.
Assess the validity of the claimed 40% improvement by reviewing reconciliation tool logs and baseline reports.
Ensure month‑end close notes include all required fields (carried‑over breaks, reasons, analyst ownership).
hiringEvidencePacket.auditSummary: The candidate demonstrates strong process ownership and documentation skills relevant to the role, but lacks verifiable evidence of measurable improvement in settlement break clearance time. Human review should focus on obtaining quantitative metrics and confirming the candidate’s understanding of baseline data.
limitations: Analysis limited to provided resume, work samples, and notes; no external data or interview transcripts were available.
